guide.title: Old Toccoa Farm: Golf in Mineral Bluff, Georgia
guide.intro: Golf Digest's 2025-'26 ranking of the best golf courses in Georgia runs as a countdown of forty entries, and a traveller with no membership, no resort booking and no host relationship has to go thirty-six entries down it before reaching a course that will sell them a tee time. That course is number 37, Old Toccoa Farm, in Mineral Bluff, in Fannin County in the north Georgia mountains, and it is what this guide is about. The ranking page dates itself in its own words: "Below you'll find our 2025-'26 ranking of the Best Golf Courses in Georgia." No other state in this set of guides required a walk anything like this deep. Every entry above #37 fails one of two tests — the ranking's own access label, or the operator's own terms for how a stranger gets on the tee. Thirty-one of them, #1 Augusta National Golf Club down to #31 The Standard Club, carry a "Private" rubric and stop at the first test. #32 Currahee Club carries "Public" and fails the second: its own site is titled "Currahee Club | Private Golf & Lake Community in Georgia." #23 The McLemore Club: Highlands offers three routes onto its course and every one of them is an affiliation, a hotel stay or a membership. #36 Reynolds Lake Oconee: The National carries no access label at all. Old Toccoa Farm is the first entry in the countdown that passes both tests, and its operator says so in its own words: "public play is welcomed six days a week."

sections.heading: Getting there
sections.body:
Old Toccoa Farm is at 596 Curtis Switch Road, Mineral Bluff, GA 30559, telephone 706-946-4653. The entrance road is Old Toccoa Way; routing software asked for the operator's own published coordinate returns that road name as the destination, snapped 4.0 metres from the point the resort's own embedded map link uses. The course sits in unincorporated Fannin County: the US Census geocoder, queried at that coordinate, returns County "Fannin County" and County Subdivision "Mineral Bluff CCD" and returns no incorporated place at all. That absence is real rather than a geocoder failure — the same query run at Blue Ridge, the Fannin County seat and the nearest incorporated city, returns "Blue Ridge city." Mineral Bluff is the postal and census subdivision name here, not a city limit.

By road from Chattanooga Metropolitan Airport (CHA), Chattanooga, Tennessee: 70.8 miles. The route leaves the airport on Airport Perimeter Road, takes TN 153 and I-75, then US 64 / US 74 (Waterlevel Highway, the longest single leg at 33.05 miles), continues on US 74, crosses into Georgia onto SR 68, then GA 60 (Mineral Bluff Highway) and Toccoa Avenue, and finishes on Curtis Switch Road.

By road from Hartsfield-Jackson Atlanta International Airport (ATL), the largest hub serving the state: 110.0 miles. That route runs I-75 north (Horace E Tate Freeway, then Larry McDonald Memorial Highway), then I-575 / GA 5 (A.P.D. Highway and the Phillip Landrum Memorial Highway, 24.21 miles), continues on GA 515 / US 76 / GA 2 / GA 5 and GA 5 (Blue Ridge Drive), then Dills Road to Curtis Switch Road.

Parking is constrained if you stay on the property, and the resort states the limit rather than leaving it to be discovered: "The maximum parking limit at The Hillside Cottages is ONE (1) VEHICLE," and those cottages have "a maximum occupancy of TWO (2) Guests." A foursome arriving in four cars needs to read that page before booking.

sections.heading: The walk down to #37
sections.body:
Golf Digest's Georgia page renders as a countdown — #40 first in document order, #1 last — and carries forty entries with no gaps and no duplicates. Read from the top, #1 Augusta National Golf Club, #2 Peachtree Golf Club, #3 Ohoopee Match Club, #4 East Lake Golf Club and every entry down to #31 The Standard Club: Standard carry the rubric "Private." Two entries above the chosen course deserve their own paragraph, and one of them is the reason the walk goes as far as it does.

#32 Currahee Club, Toccoa, is the clearest case in this set of a ranking label and an operator disagreeing. The ranking gives it "Public." Its own homepage is titled "Currahee Club | Private Golf & Lake Community in Georgia" and states that "Currahee Club is managed by Troon Privé, bringing the expertise and resources of a global leader in private club management to the Currahee community." The site sells membership and nothing else: six categories — Resident Golf, Resident Social, Non-Resident Social, Non-Resident Golf ("For those who own or lease real estate within 35 miles of the Currahee Club"), Regional ("within 35 to 150 miles from the club") and National ("more than 150 miles from the club"). The only non-member route onto the course it describes anywhere is a sales visit: "Prospective members can arrange a private visit to tour the clubhouse and amenities, meet the membership team, dine at the club and play a round on Currahee's Jim Fazio-designed golf course." Its course page publishes yardage under "Championship Tees" and "Member Tees" and carries no green fee, no rate table and no tee-time link; its own page sitemap lists fourteen pages and none of them is a rates page, a tee-times page or a stay-and-play page. There is no booking system to overrule the marketing copy. And the same publisher labelled the same club "Private" at #21 in the archived 2023-'24 edition of this ranking, so the contradiction is not only between publisher and operator but between one edition and the next.

#23 The McLemore Club: Highlands, Rising Fawn, is the entry most likely to be argued as a mislabelled public course, so it was checked against its operator rather than against its label. The club's golf page reads: "THREE WAYS TO PLAY AT MCLEMORE. We have designed three ways for you to enjoy the McLemore golf experience. The first and easiest way is as a Friend of McLemore, the second is as a Stay & Play or Cloudland hotel guest, and the third is as a Member of our Highlands Course or The Keep." The first of those is an accepted invitation good for play "once each season." An affiliation, a hotel booking or a membership — all three are gates, and McLemore does not clear the bar this guide applies.

#36 Reynolds Lake Oconee: The National (Ridge/Bluff) is recorded here as what it is on the page: an entry whose own block carries a bare token where every other entry carries "Public" or "Private," with no city line, no rating and no blurb. That is an observed absence in the source, not a label borrowed from a neighbour.

This guide does not rest on counting how many entries carry a "Public" rubric, because that field moves. Archived captures of this same 2025-'26 edition, parsed by binding each rubric to its own entry block, show #23 McLemore carrying "Public" in captures dated 16 June 2025, 11 February 2026 and 8 March 2026 — above the chosen course — and show #32 Currahee carrying "Private" in the 16 June 2025 capture. The archived 2023-'24 edition of the same page holds 35 entries, every one of them "Private," and Old Toccoa Farm does not appear in it at all. What makes the walk end at #37 is not a label count on any one day; it is that every entry above it fails either the ranking's own label or the operator's own terms, McLemore included. Golf Digest separately publishes a "best public courses in Georgia" collection whose entries include Sea Island: Seaside, Reynolds Lake Oconee: Great Waters, The McLemore Club: Highlands and Currahee Club — four courses the same publisher's state ranking labels Private, Private, Private and Public. That collection is looser than the bar used here and decided nothing in this guide; it is named because it is the likeliest source of a contrary claim.

sections.heading: Old Toccoa Farm
sections.body:
Eighteen holes above the Toccoa River, at #37 on Golf Digest's 2025-'26 Georgia ranking with a panelist rating of 3.6 from 10 panelists and the access label "Public." The operator credits "the Jack Dredla, Dan Proctor, Dave Axland, aka Bunker Hill-designed course"; Golf Digest's own course page for it lists "Designer Dan Proctor/Dave Axland." Both credits are recorded here and neither is reconciled into the other.

The chronology, quoted from that Golf Digest course page: "Work on Old Toccoa Farm started during the financial crisis. After nine holes originally opened in 2015, Dan Proctor and Dave Axland, a long-time shaper for Bill Coore and Crenshaw, finalized their design in 2020, earning recognition with a top-10 award in Golf Digest's Best New survey. The course features 300 feet of elevation change and stunning views of the surrounding Chattahoochee and Cherokee National Forests." The operator states the placing more precisely than its publisher does — "#8 Best New Course in America, 2020 – Golf Digest" — and that number rests on the operator's own assertion, because the 2020 list itself was not retrieved for this guide. Golf Digest's own wording is "a top-10 award."

Surfaces and shape, from the operator: "Tightly mowed zoysia fairways and manicured bentgrass greens create an incredible surface for play as the course winds along the river valley and into the landscape's secluded hills and draws. Native grasses, wicked bunkers, and exceptional long-range mountain views complete the experience." A Golf Digest panelist gives the dimensions: "A par 72, 6700-yard course from the tips and 4,500 from the forward tees." Another panelist notes that "A double green for holes 14 & 16 makes for fun routing." The property around it is the operator's own description: "Our 420+ acre property… sits between expansive protected forest lands filled with twisted knots of mountain laurel, meadows of native grasses, and over 4,000+ feet of frontage along the Toccoa River."

Old Toccoa Farm is not on the National Register of Historic Places, and that is a checked negative rather than an omission: the National Register listing for Fannin County, Georgia, complete through National Park Service listings posted 4 September 2026, holds exactly four properties — the James W. Baugh Homeplace, the Blue Ridge Depot, the Fannin County Courthouse and the Mineral Bluff Depot. The operator claims no designation, and its "protected forest lands" phrasing describes the adjoining national forest, not the course.

sections.heading: Playing it
sections.body:
The operator states the access terms in its own words, on two separate pages. From the golf page: "Old Toccoa Farm is a semi-private course where public play is welcomed six days a week. All public players must call ahead to make a tee time. Public tee times can be made no sooner than 7 days ahead of the preferred day unless you are reserving accommodations here at Old Toccoa Farm Resort." From the membership page, under its own heading PUBLIC PLAY: "Public play is welcome at Old Toccoa Farm. Golfers can reserve tee times a week in advance. Callaway rental clubs are available. PROPER ATTIRE IS REQUIRED / NO JEANS. CELL PHONES SILENT AT ALL TIMES. NO COOLERS & NO ALCOHOLIC BEVERAGES."

The packages page draws the distinction that matters, in a package's own inclusion list: "Priority Tee Time Access: Reserve as far in advance as you like" against "Tee Times for Guests Not Staying on Property: Released only 7 days prior." Staying on the property buys an earlier booking window, not entry. Somebody with no membership, no lodging booking and no host can play, at a seven-day booking horizon.

There is no online tee-time engine, and that is reported as an absence rather than assumed. The "MAKE A TEE TIME" element on the site is a heading, not a link — the markup is literally "MAKE A TEE TIME 706-946-4653" inside an h2 — and the golf page's only booking control is a telephone link reading "Call for a tee time: 706-946-GOLF." The one external commerce link on the site opens an apparel shop whose own front page reads "Welcome to our online store! Orders typically ship in 5-10 business days"; it is not a tee sheet. Booking here is a phone call.

Hours and conditions, quoted: "The Golf Course Hours are 8:00 am - 5:00 pm (Closed Tuesday). Rates include greens fee, cart fee, range balls and taxes. Practice facilities, including driving range, chipping and putting greens, open to all golfers with scheduled tee times only." The published holiday block is "Thanksgiving Day: Closed / Christmas Eve: Golf Shop closing at 2:00 PM / Christmas Day: Closed / NYE & NYD: Normal Operating Hours." No seasonal shutdown is stated anywhere on the site, and no aeration, renovation, flood or maintenance notice was found on it.

This guide publishes no green fee for Old Toccoa Farm. The operator does print a rate table, but it carries no dated qualifier of any kind — no season year, no "effective" line, nothing that fixes the numbers to a period. The only date attached to that page anywhere is the content management system's own page-modified timestamp, which records when the page was edited and not when the rates took effect, and the site footer's copyright line is older still. Golf Digest's course page echoes a single price with the note "This covers all ranges of greens fees. Please check with the course on specific timing and pricing," which is a third-party echo and does not cure the absence. Ask for the rate on the same call that books the tee time.

The resort publishes a live events calendar, and it is worth reading before choosing a date. It lists a Club Championship on 12 and 13 September 2026, described on its own page as a "2 DAY EVENT (SEPTEMBER 12 & 13) Member Only Event" of "Two days. Thirty-six holes of stroke play"; a Member-Guest Tournament on 2 to 4 October 2026; and five more dated tournaments — the Blue Ridge Medical Center Foundation Pink & White Classic on 17 October, the Chamber of Commerce Tournament on 20 October, the Mountain Lion Club Scholarship Tournament on 2 November, the MGA ETC Memorial Tournament on 7 November and the Toys for Tots Tournament on 30 November 2026. None of those pages says the course is closed to outside play on those dates, and this guide does not say so either; what is on the record is that a member-only 36-hole championship occupies a full weekend and that six further tournaments occupy dated blocks. The telephone number above will settle it.

sections.heading: The weekend around the course
sections.body:
Lodging on the property runs through one named partner, and the resort says so: "Escape to Blue Ridge is the exclusive hospitality partner for Old Toccoa Farm Resort and manages all overnight accommodations on property." Two routes are described. A Standard Resort Stay is "Flexible. Independent. Book online… reserve any golf, dining, or resort activities independently," and includes "Flexible stay duration in any of our guest accommodations; Advance tee time access; Convenient access to resort amenities." A Stay & Play Package is "Available only on select dates; packages must be booked for designated stay dates," and includes "Two Nights in a Hillside Cottage – Extended Stays Welcomed," a "Saturday round of golf for two," advance tee time access, a "$100 Food & Beverage Credit at The Tavern," and early arrival with late check-out. The packages page is explicit about how to buy one: "All packages are booked by calling our exclusive hospitality partner Escape to Blue Ridge at 866.618.2521."

The Hillside Cottages are the couples option and the harder-constrained one. The resort describes them as "designed by Patrick Kirkland with Kirkland & Associates Architecture, and interiors designed by Vicki Decker, owner of New Blue Home and Gift, a Blue Ridge design firm," with "cozy living rooms… full kitchens complete with quartz countertops and bar seating… a wine fridge, ice maker, oven, microwave, Nespresso Coffeemaker, and a washer/dryer," and "a separate bedroom with a king-size bed and a private bath with a tiled shower." Outside, "Two Adirondack chairs provide a comfortable spot to take in the view of the award-winning golf course and the Toccoa River." The hard limits are the ones in Getting there: one vehicle, two guests.

For a group, Bunker Down — the resort's guest residence — holds "accommodations for eight guests with a designer kitchen, five bedrooms, large outdoor living spaces, a washer and dryer and gathering areas," is "located at Old Toccoa Farm… overlooking the 6th hole," and adds "a screened porch, comfortable beds and en-suite bathrooms… a fireplace and 65" Smart TV… a six-person hot tub, a cozy chaise lounge, a gas grill, and a cornhole set."

Eating is one room, and it is open to people who are neither staying nor playing. The Tavern at Old Toccoa Farm "offers members and visiting guests a casual, yet elegant dining experience with views of the 9th hole, the Toccoa River valley, and the distant Blue Ridge Mountains. Dining areas include large, covered patios, an indoor and outdoor bar area, and a private room for 25+ people, with fireplace." On access it is unambiguous: "We are open to the public, and reservations are required via phone or online." Reservations run through Resy. Published hours are Monday, Wednesday, Thursday and Friday — lunch 11:00 AM to 4:00 PM, social hour 3:00 to 5:00 PM, dinner 4:00 to 9:00 PM; Saturday and Sunday — brunch 9:00 AM to 4:00 PM, social hour 2:00 to 5:00 PM, dinner 4:00 to 9:00 PM; Tuesday closed, the same day the course is. Two brunch items as the menu lists them: "AVOCADO TOAST $15 — Goat Cheese Crumble | Pickled Onions | Pickled Tomato | Everything Seasoning" and "BISCUITS & HONEY $12 — Honey Butter | Apple Butter | Jams & Jellies." The pet policy is stated: "dogs and other pets are not permitted inside the restaurant or on the dining patio. Service animals, as defined by the ADA, are always welcome."

Off the property, the resort positions itself relative to downtown Blue Ridge, which is the Fannin County seat and the nearest incorporated city to the course. This guide names no restaurant or hotel there, because the research established none by name.

sections.heading: Day two: Copper Basin Golf Club
sections.body:
The second course is the nearest publicly accessible one by road, and the rule that picks it takes no account of state lines. That is Copper Basin Golf Club, at 5765 Highway 64, Copperhill, Tennessee 37317-6412, telephone 423-496-3579, and it is 10.6 road miles from Old Toccoa Farm. The route leaves on Old Toccoa Way and Curtis Switch Road, runs GA 60 (Mineral Bluff Highway) for 4.01 miles and Pleasant Hill Road for 3.31 miles, takes Wolf Creek Road for 0.20 miles and finishes on West US 64 / US 74 for 1.47 miles. Its own county is Polk County, Tennessee — the Census geocoder, run at the club's geocoded street address, returns State "Tennessee," County "Polk County," County Subdivision "District 3" and, as at Old Toccoa Farm, no incorporated place. Controls run inside the same county return "Ducktown city" and "Benton town," so that absence is real too. A sweep of every mapped golf course within 60 km of Old Toccoa Farm found nothing at all between the chosen course and Copper Basin; the next candidate after it is at 12.9 straight-line miles.

Its access was established by executing its booking system rather than by reading its adjectives. Copper Basin books through Club Caddie. Bootstrapping a session against the club's own public tee sheet and posting that sheet's own search form returned 83 distinct bookable tee times for Saturday 12 September 2026, from 08:00 AM to 06:56 PM, each carrying a live "Book Now" control. The rate classes offered online are named only Weekend, Weekday and Twilight; the strings "Member" and "Senior" do not appear in the returned rate objects at all, so no member-restricted class is sold online. And there is no login wall on the control that books: in the returned markup the login-gated variants of the "Book Now" button are commented out, while the live control is a plain form submit. Login and registration are offered, not required, to reach the booking post. The operator's own homepage puts it in one line: "Originally built for the Copper Company, our course has evolved into a beloved public destination known for its rolling Bermuda fairways, challenging Bentgrass greens, and breathtaking mountain views." Membership exists, is sold as an optional retail product beside an explicit "Non-Member" rate row, and gates nothing.

One thing about that tee sheet needs saying plainly, because it is easy to misread. The sheet returns bookable times for a band of dates and nothing outside it, and the band is bounded at both ends relative to the day you ask: yesterday and last month return zero, the sheet for the day you ask on is truncated to times still ahead on the clock, and the far edge sits 30 days out from the query. That is how far ahead the system takes bookings — a rolling 30-day window — and it is not a closure. The club publishes no closure, aeration, renovation, flood or maintenance notice anywhere on its site, in visible text or in HTML comments, and its events calendar is published and genuinely empty.

The course itself is nine holes, and the operator's own account of its age is inconsistent with itself: the homepage says "a favorite for over 85 years" and the rates page says "For over 100 years, Copper Basin Golf Club has offered a welcoming, memorable golf experience." Both are the operator's and neither is reconciled here. No architect is named anywhere on the site. The club is under new ownership and posts a notice about it: "Pardon Our Construction — You may notice some construction around the course as our new ownership rolls up their sleeves to make Copper Basin Golf Club even better. As a local family with deep roots in this community, we're investing in the improvements this course deserves, all while keeping the charm that's made it a favorite for over 85 years." Its facilities page frames pickleball courts, an enhanced range and two simulator rooms as "Coming Soon to CBGC." Nothing on the site says holes are out of play, and the tee sheet returned full days across its whole window.

No green fee is published here for Copper Basin either. Its printed rate card carries no dated qualifier — the only four-digit year anywhere on that page is the footer copyright — and the prices its booking engine quotes are engine output, not a dated rate. Both courses in this guide therefore go without a printed price, which is the rule working rather than a gap in the research. The nearest Georgia alternative, for a traveller who would rather not cross the state line, is Whitepath Golf Club at 1156 Shenandoa Drive, Ellijay, in Gilmer County, 17.7 road miles from Old Toccoa Farm; it describes itself as "a public golf course located 5 miles north of Ellijay, Georgia," books online through a public tee-time class that needs no authentication, and is the one course in this research whose greens-fee card is dated by its own heading. It is farther than Copper Basin, so it is not this guide's second course.

faq.question: How do I book a tee time at Old Toccoa Farm?
faq.answer: By telephone. There is no online tee-time engine: the "MAKE A TEE TIME" element on the site is a heading rather than a link, and the golf page's only booking control is a telephone link reading "Call for a tee time: 706-946-GOLF" — 706-946-4653. The operator's terms: "All public players must call ahead to make a tee time. Public tee times can be made no sooner than 7 days ahead of the preferred day unless you are reserving accommodations here at Old Toccoa Farm Resort."

faq.question: Do I have to stay on the property or join to play?
faq.answer: No. The operator calls it "a semi-private course where public play is welcomed six days a week," and its membership page carries a PUBLIC PLAY heading of its own: "Public play is welcome at Old Toccoa Farm. Golfers can reserve tee times a week in advance." What staying on the property buys is an earlier booking window, not entry — the packages page sets "Priority Tee Time Access: Reserve as far in advance as you like" against "Tee Times for Guests Not Staying on Property: Released only 7 days prior."

faq.question: What does a round cost?
faq.answer: This guide publishes no green fee for Old Toccoa Farm or for Copper Basin, because neither operator dates its rate card. Old Toccoa Farm prints a rate table with no season year, no "effective" line and no other qualifier that fixes the numbers to a period; the only date on the page is a page-edit timestamp from its content management system, which is not a rate-effective date. Copper Basin's card is the same, with a footer copyright as the only year on the page. What the Old Toccoa Farm page does state about what the number covers is quotable: "Rates include greens fee, cart fee, range balls and taxes." Ask for the figure on the call that books the tee time.

faq.question: Which day is the course closed?
faq.answer: Tuesday. The operator publishes "The Golf Course Hours are 8:00 am - 5:00 pm (Closed Tuesday)" and repeats it in the site footer. The published holiday block is "Thanksgiving Day: Closed / Christmas Eve: Golf Shop closing at 2:00 PM / Christmas Day: Closed / NYE & NYD: Normal Operating Hours." No seasonal shutdown is stated anywhere on the site, and no aeration, renovation or maintenance notice was found. The Tavern is closed Tuesdays as well.

faq.question: Should I avoid particular dates?
faq.answer: The resort's own events calendar lists a member-only Club Championship on 12 and 13 September 2026 — "2 DAY EVENT (SEPTEMBER 12 & 13) Member Only Event," thirty-six holes of stroke play — a Member-Guest Tournament on 2 to 4 October 2026, and five further dated tournaments: 17 October, 20 October, 2 November, 7 November and 30 November 2026. None of those pages says outside play is suspended, and this guide does not claim it is. It is a reason to telephone before fixing one of those dates.

faq.question: Where exactly is Old Toccoa Farm?
faq.answer: 596 Curtis Switch Road, Mineral Bluff, GA 30559, in unincorporated Fannin County, in the north Georgia mountains. The US Census geocoder, run at the operator's own published coordinate, returns County "Fannin County" and County Subdivision "Mineral Bluff CCD" and returns no incorporated place; the same query at Blue Ridge, the county seat, returns "Blue Ridge city," which is how the absence was shown to be real. By road it is 70.8 miles from Chattanooga Metropolitan Airport (CHA) and 110.0 miles from Hartsfield-Jackson Atlanta International Airport (ATL).

faq.question: Where should I play on day two?
faq.answer: Copper Basin Golf Club, nine holes at 5765 Highway 64, Copperhill, Tennessee, 10.6 road miles from Old Toccoa Farm by way of GA 60, Pleasant Hill Road, Wolf Creek Road and US 64 / US 74. It is the nearest publicly accessible course, and the rule that picks it does not stop at the state line. Its access is not an adjective: its public tee sheet, queried for Saturday 12 September 2026, returned 83 bookable tee times from 08:00 AM to 06:56 PM under rate classes named only Weekend, Weekday and Twilight, with no member-restricted class sold online and the login-gated booking buttons commented out of the page.

faq.question: Copper Basin's booking page shows nothing past a certain date. Is the course closing?
faq.answer: No. That is how far ahead the system takes bookings. The window is bounded at both ends relative to the day you ask: yesterday and last month return no times at all, the sheet for the day you ask on is truncated to times still ahead on the clock, and the far edge sits 30 days out from the query. A closure cannot produce a lower bound that moves with the clock. The club publishes no closure notice of any kind, and its events calendar is empty.

faq.question: Is Old Toccoa Farm really the highest-ranked course in Georgia a visitor can play?
faq.answer: It is the highest-ranked publicly accessible course on Golf Digest's 2025-'26 Best in State ranking for Georgia, at #37 of 40, on the bar this guide applies: no membership, no resort booking, no host relationship. Every entry above it fails either the ranking's own access label or its operator's own terms — #32 Currahee Club carries a "Public" rubric while its own site is titled "Private Golf & Lake Community" and sells only membership categories, and #23 The McLemore Club: Highlands offers three routes onto the course, all of them an affiliation, a hotel stay or a membership. The rubric field itself moves between captures of the same edition, so the claim here rests on the operators' terms rather than on counting labels.

faq.question: Where do I eat?
faq.answer: The Tavern at Old Toccoa Farm, on the property, with "views of the 9th hole, the Toccoa River valley, and the distant Blue Ridge Mountains." It states its own access: "We are open to the public, and reservations are required via phone or online," through Resy. Lunch runs 11:00 AM to 4:00 PM Monday, Wednesday, Thursday and Friday, with dinner 4:00 to 9:00 PM; weekend brunch runs 9:00 AM to 4:00 PM with dinner 4:00 to 9:00 PM. Closed Tuesdays. Dogs are not permitted inside or on the dining patio; ADA service animals are welcome.

places.name: Old Toccoa Farm
places.summary: #37 of 40 on Golf Digest's 2025-'26 ranking of the best golf courses in Georgia, rated 3.6 by 10 panelists and labelled "Public" — the first entry in that countdown a visitor with no membership, resort booking or host can play. Eighteen holes above the Toccoa River on a 420+ acre property, credited by the operator to "Jack Dredla, Dan Proctor, Dave Axland, aka Bunker Hill" and by Golf Digest to "Dan Proctor/Dave Axland." Nine holes opened in 2015 and the design was finalized in 2020; 300 feet of elevation change, zoysia fairways and bentgrass greens, par 72 at 6,700 yards from the tips and 4,500 from the forward tees, with a double green shared by holes 14 and 16. Booking is by telephone, 706-946-4653; public tee times open seven days ahead. Closed Tuesdays.

places.name: Copper Basin Golf Club
places.summary: Nine holes at 5765 Highway 64, Copperhill, in unincorporated Polk County, Tennessee, 10.6 road miles from Old Toccoa Farm and the nearest publicly accessible course to it in any direction. The operator: "Originally built for the Copper Company, our course has evolved into a beloved public destination known for its rolling Bermuda fairways, challenging Bentgrass greens, and breathtaking mountain views." Its Club Caddie tee sheet, queried for Saturday 12 September 2026, returned 83 bookable tee times from 08:00 AM to 06:56 PM under rate classes named only Weekend, Weekday and Twilight, with no member-restricted class online and the login-gated booking buttons commented out of the markup. Membership is sold as an optional product beside an explicit "Non-Member" rate row. No architect is named on the site, and the operator's own account of its age varies between "over 85 years" and "over 100 years."

places.name: The Tavern at Old Toccoa Farm
places.summary: The resort's dining room, with "views of the 9th hole, the Toccoa River valley, and the distant Blue Ridge Mountains," covered patios, indoor and outdoor bars and a private room for 25 or more. Access in the operator's own words: "We are open to the public, and reservations are required via phone or online," through Resy. Lunch 11:00 AM to 4:00 PM and dinner 4:00 to 9:00 PM Monday, Wednesday, Thursday and Friday; brunch 9:00 AM to 4:00 PM and dinner 4:00 to 9:00 PM Saturday and Sunday; closed Tuesday. Dogs are not permitted inside or on the dining patio; ADA service animals are welcome.

places.name: The Hillside Cottages
places.summary: On-property lodging at Old Toccoa Farm, managed — like all overnight accommodation here — by the resort's exclusive hospitality partner, Escape to Blue Ridge, 866.618.2521. The operator describes cottages "designed by Patrick Kirkland with Kirkland & Associates Architecture," with interiors by Vicki Decker of New Blue Home and Gift, full kitchens with quartz countertops, a wine fridge, ice maker, Nespresso coffeemaker and washer/dryer, a separate king bedroom and a tiled shower, and two Adirondack chairs facing the course and the Toccoa River. Hard limits from the resort's own policy page: one vehicle per cottage and a maximum occupancy of two guests.

places.name: Bunker Down
places.summary: The group option on the property: a guest residence sleeping eight in five bedrooms, overlooking the 6th hole, with a designer kitchen, en-suite bathrooms, a screened porch, a fireplace, a six-person hot tub, a gas grill and a cornhole set. Booked, like every other room here, through Escape to Blue Ridge at 866.618.2521.

entries.name: Old Toccoa Farm

entries.note: Day two: nine holes in Copperhill, Tennessee, 10.6 road miles away and the nearest publicly accessible course, with 83 bookable tee times returned for Saturday 12 September 2026.

entries.name: The Tavern at Old Toccoa Farm
entries.note: "We are open to the public, and reservations are required via phone or online." Closed Tuesday, the same day as the course.

entries.name: The Hillside Cottages
entries.note: On-property cottages booked through Escape to Blue Ridge at 866.618.2521; one vehicle and two guests maximum.

entries.name: Bunker Down
entries.note: Five bedrooms sleeping eight, overlooking the 6th hole, for a group booking through the same partner line.
